about: Which audiences are given RS256 and what discovery lists (ADR 0006, "Named exceptions"; REQ-KEYS-005, REQ-CLIENT-046, REQ-TOKEN-043, REQ-TOKEN-044, REQ-AUTHN-108). Each audience is a client. v1 pins signing_alg on a client row and keeps one default for every other; v2 keeps that and narrows it: the RSA key signs ID tokens only, for an audience that says RS256 in so many words, never by the caller's choice, and an audience whose key is not live is refused and never given ES384. Names are made up (example.org). actors/store is held to "config", actors/signer to "tokens" and actors/entry to "discovery".

config.about: What the loader takes as a client's signing_alg (REQ-CLIENT-046). value is the YAML scalar as written; absent means the key is left out. alg is what the loader records ('' is the default, ES384). A word outside the closed list is refused at the field with no value in the message: class 'value' is a string that is none of '', ES384 and RS256 (case and spaces count), 'type' is not a string, 'exchange' is any algorithm on a client that is given access tokens only.

tokens.about: What signer signs for an audience. signing_alg is the client's, as the loader stored it ('' is the default); typ is JWT for an ID token and at+jwt for an access token; rs256_key is the state of the RS256 purpose: 'unlisted' (the KeyPlan does not list it), 'listed, no key' (it lists it and key@ has none), 'pre-published' (the key waits for its lead time), 'active', 'revoked' (KeyRevocation lists its kid). The answer is alg, the algorithm in the header, or refused with the closed reason signer audits and no token of another algorithm. session and exchange get the same answer. A signing_alg that is not in the closed list cannot come from a loader; signer still signs no ID token for it (the second line).

discovery.about: What the discovery document lists in id_token_signing_alg_values_supported and whether the key set holds the RSA key (REQ-AUTHN-108, REQ-KEYS-271). rs256_key is the state of the ring's RSA key, null for a ring with none; revoked is whether KeyRevocation lists its kid; revocations says whether KeyRevocation can be read. The document lists ES384 always and RS256 only while the ring holds an active RS256 key that is not revoked: an installation with no RSA key serves no RS256. The key set holds the RSA key in every published state (pre-published, active, retiring) as an RSA entry with n and e and no x5c, and is withheld (503) when the revocations cannot be read.
